Highlights (key summary)
▪ In October 2026:
⎯ A total of Two Hundred and Twenty (220) suspected dengue fever cases were reported from 
3 states (Akwa-ibom, Sokoto and Zamfara State) in October 2026.
⎯ Seventeen (17) cases, representing 7.7% of the suspected cases, were confirmed by laboratory 
testing.
⎯ Eight (8) Local Government Areas (LGA), 4 in Sokoto State (Bodginga – 6, Dange-Shuni –
1, Isa – 2 and Tambuwal - 1), 1 in Akwa – Ibom (Uyo), and 3 in Zamfara (Birnin Magaji –
71, Zurmi – 91 and Shinkafi - 47) reported the suspected case of dengue fever.
⎯ Three (3) deaths was recorded among the confirmed cases.
⎯ CFR – 17.6%
▪ From January – October 2026:
⎯ A total of 10 states have reported dengue fever cases. With new cases coming from Zamfara 
State(366) and Akwa-ibom (1).
⎯ Zamfara (366), Edo (55) and Sokoto State (49) jointly accounted for 89.9% of the 523
suspected cases reported.
⎯ Of the suspected cases, 34 (6.5%) were confirmed.
⎯ The young and middle aged adults of age group 21 to 50 yrs with 19 cases accounts for 55.9% 
of all 34 confirmed cases. 
⎯ A total of 4 deaths were recorded among confirmed cases, representing a case fatality rate
(CFR) of 11.8%
▪ Overview from Jan 2025 till date(October, 2026):
⎯ Edo (600), Zamfara (366), Sokoto (160) Gombe (57) and Delta State (50) jointly accounted for 
97% of the 1271 suspected cases reported.
⎯ Of the suspected cases, 255 (20.1%) were confirmed.

Challenges
• Low awareness of dengue fever case definition among healthcare workers, leading to late diagnosis
• Insufficient vector control at the community level
• Inadequate public awareness of dengue symptoms and prevention
• Poor waste management creates mosquito breeding sites
Recommendations
▪ Validate and disseminate the drafted guidelines on dengue fever surveillance
▪ Ensure timely resore of stockout reagents
▪ Facilitate the training of healthcare workers on dengue fever case identification and management
▪ Follow up with states in outbreak for ongoing response activities and challenges in the various states
▪ Follow up with states (State Epids and SSO) and reference laboratories on using SORMAS in timely 
collecting and transmitting surveillance and laboratory data respectively.
▪ Weekly dengue fever surveillance data review.
